*****NOTE FROM THE CITY: PUBLIC PARTICIPATION: Due to the existing COVID-19
health emergency and the social distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant to
the Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20 (https://www.gov.ca.gov/wp-
content/uploads/2020/03/3.17.20-N-29-20-EO.pdf).

Please note that members of the public will be allowed to observe and/or address the City
Council Meeting of June 8, 2021, at 2:00 P.M. for open session as follows:

  1.  Written Public Comments: Members of the public may choose to submit
  comments electronically for consideration by the Inglewood City Council/Successor
  Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority/Parking Authority/Joint Powers
  Authority (Legislative Body) by sending them to the City Clerk/Secretary at
  athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at
  aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the members of the
  Legislative Body prior to consideration of the agenda, please submit comments
  prior to 8:00 A.M. the day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify
  the agenda number or subject matter. Correspondence should indicate the meeting
  date and agenda item. Comments received after 8:00 A.M. and prior to the close of
  the public hearings, will be made part of the official public record of the meeting.
  Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

  2.  By Telephone-Listening to the Meeting and Making Oral Public
  Comments: Members of the public can participate in the meeting by telephone to
  listen and make comments noting the following:

  l  The conference begins at 1:30 p.m., Pacific Time, and all interested parties may
  join the conference 5 minutes prior.
   2.  By Telephone-Listening to the Meeting and Making Oral Public
  Comments: Members of the public can participate in the meeting by telephone to
  listen and make comments noting the following:

  l  The conference begins at 1:30 p.m., Pacific Time, and all interested parties may
  join the conference 5 minutes prior.
  l  If you are dialing in from a cell phone, please call from an area with good
  reception. Calls from landline phones are highly recommended.
  l  If you are watching the meeting via Social Media or Channel 35 while also
  accessing the phone line, it is requested that you mute the sound of your video
  feed as it is delayed from the phone transmission. Additionally, when you are
  making public comments on the phone line, you will be inaudible due to
  feedback.
  l  Dial-In: 1-888-251-2949 or 1-215-861-0694 using the specific access codes
  detailed below for the respective City Council Dates:
  l June 8, 2021 – Access Code: 5362462# wait two seconds and press #
  again
  l  June 15, 2021 – Access Code: 4755419# wait two seconds and press #
  again
  l  June 22, 2021 – Access Code: 4500707# wait two seconds and press #
  again
  l  June 29, 2021 – Access Code: 4731505# wait two seconds and press #
  again

  3.  Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:

  l  On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please check with
  your cable provider for details.

The above access options provide the public with the opportunity to both observe and
listen to the meeting; however, members of the public who wish to orally address the
Legislative Body must use the public access options 1 and 2 noted above.

ACCESSIBILITY: If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in
appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability, as required by Section 202 of
the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (42 U.S.C. Sec. 12132), and the federal rules and
regulations adopted in implementation thereof. Any person who requires a disability-
related modification or accommodation, or translation services in order to observe and/or
offer public comment may request such reasonable modification, accommodation, or
service by contacting the Office of the City Clerk by telephone at 310-412-5280, FAX at
310-412-5533, One Manchester Boulevard, First Floor, Inglewood City Hall, Inglewood, CA
90301 or via email to athompson@cityofinglewood.org and aallen@cityofinglewood.org
no later than 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting.

Inglewood, California
  June 8, 2021

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  June 8, 2021, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
  City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority at the
  hour of 2:00 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
  presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members Dotson, Padilla,
  Morales, and Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as
  follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority.
  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS.  Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
  who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any
  item on the Agendas.
  Gil Mathieu, District 4, commented on the Warrants and Bills.

  Caller (Name Unknown) commented on the Warrants and Bills, and Agenda Item Nos. 4,
  5, 6, SPH-1, and DR-1.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Faulk that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated June
  4, 2021, in the amount of $5,238,781.69, and dated May 27, 2021, in the amount of
  $1,877,411.08 are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency
  Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said registers
  that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call
  vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council
  Member Dotson that the Minutes for the City Council Meeting held on November 17,
  2020, be approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Abstain: Council Member Faulk.

  CLAIMS DENIED. Letters from the Office of the City Attorney recommending the
  following:
  A. Reject Claim filed pursuant to Government Code Section 913:
   June 8, 2021

  1. Wilfredo Cardenas for alleged property damage and personal injury; crashed into
  metal barricades near SoFi Stadium on December 6, 2020.
  2. Manuel Duskin for alleged personal injury; trip on pothole on March 17, 2021.
  3. Tabitha Gilmore for alleged tire damage; pothole on February 11, 2021.
  4. Robert Marvray for alleged vehicle damage; pothole on March 3, 2021.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby reject claims listed as A-1 through A-4. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

171  PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – L.A. BUSINESS PRINTING SERVICES. Staff report
  dated June 8, 2021, was presented recommending authorization to pay the invoice
  submitted by L.A. Business Printing Services for additional work required for publication
  of the Community Information Guide.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby authorize payment in the amount of $16,622.33. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

171  PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – SCULPTURE CONSERVATION STUDIO. Staff
  report dated June 8, 2021, was presented recommending authorization to pay the invoice
  submitted by Sculpture Conservation Studio for emergency conservation services for the
  Inglewood War Memorial (obelisk) located at City Hall South Mall.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby authorize payment in the amount of $9,130. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  COOPERATIVE PURCHASE AGREEMENT AUTHORIZED – BLACK AND
  WHITE EMERGENCY VEHICLES, LLC. Staff report dated June 8, 2021, was
  presented recommending approval of a Cooperative Purchase Agreement (includes two
  (2) one (1)-year extension options) with Black and White Emergency Vehicles, LLC for
  police vehicle up-fitting services.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that
  the City Council does hereby approve a Cooperative Purchase Agreement in an amount
  not to exceed $100,000. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  MEMORANDUM  OF  UNDERSTANDING  (MOU)  APPROVED  –
  TRANSPORTATION NETWORK COMPANY; MAYOR AUTHORIZED TO
  EXECUTE THE MOU ON BEHALF OF THE CITY. Staff report dated June 8,
  2021, was presented recommending approval of a Memorandum of Understanding
  (MOU) regarding the issuance of certain encroachment permits for Transportation
  Network Company (TNC) Activities on a monthly basis with Hollywood Park
  Management Company, LLC (HPMC), providing for the intermittent use of a public
  right-of-way area in connection with certain events held at Sofi Stadium and Hollywood
  Park and HMPC’s assumption of all liability associated therewith.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve the Memorandum of Understanding; and
  2) Authorize the Mayor to execute the MOU on behalf of the City of Inglewood. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and

  2
   June 8, 2021

  Noes:  None.

142  PUBLIC HEARING SET – AMENDING THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD MASTER
  FEE SCHEDULE; FEES AND CHARGES AUTHORIZED – FEE SCHEDULE
  FOR BUILDING SAFETY AND PLANNING. Staff report dated June 8, 2021, was
  presented requesting that a public hearing be set to receive public comments on amending
  the City of Inglewood Master Fee Schedule to reflect the suggested changes to the Fee
  Schedule for Building Safety and Planning.

  Mayor Butts ordered the public hearing set for July 13, 2021, at the hour of 2:00 p.m.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby authorize the fees and charges adjustments to come into
  effect on September 11, 2021, as set out in accordance with the findings of the User Fee
  Study. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who
  wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not
  elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  Caller (Name Unknown) spoke about Brown Act Violations, specifically regarding the
  way Council Meetings are being held. She also spoke on repairs needed on the streets and
  sidewalks in her neighborhood.

  Gil Mathieu, District 4, commented on the Warrants and Bills, and the opening of SoFi
  Stadium.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned in honor of Sargent Jakeem Vegas, nephew of Council Member Padilla, and
  Marcus Laval, Jr., father of Lori Pickens at the hour of 2:19 p.m.

  Approved this 21st day of September, 2021.

  _________________________
  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
